newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Peters says has no knowledge of SFO findings.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Peters says has no knowledge of SFO findings.

text.p: Treasurer and New Zealand First leader Winston Peters on Tuesday said he and his caucus were not aware of the contents of the Serious Fraud Office (SFO) report into Aotearoa Television Network (ATN) which they have linked to the future of errant MP Tukoroirangi Morgan.
"We are not aware of the Serious Fraud Office report and have not seen it at this point in time as I speak to you," Peters told Reuters as he left the House.
Some media commentators have suggested that NZ First leaders already know the content of the SFO report, and are speculating that it will exonerate Morgan from any criminal wrongdoing.
Peters rejected this outright.
"You are suggesting that I made the decision today with respect to the SFO report... with the knowledge of the SFO report. Nothing could be further from the truth," Peters said.
Asked if Morgan had seen the report or a draft Peters said, "No, he has not seen it to the best of my knowledge."

Earlier Peters said in a statement that Morgan's future in the NZ First party caucus would be left open until the report was handed down into the pilot Maori language network where Morgan worked before becoming an MP.
The report is expected during the next two weeks.
Morgan admitted last Thursday he had tried to sell an exclusive television interview about the ATN affair for at least NZ$20,000 to help fund two libel actions he is involved in.
He at first denied knowledge of the attempt to Peters, prompting the party leader to issue a statement of support which he later had to retract.
Peters said Morgan had apologised for his recent actions and apologised to Prime Minister Jim Bolger.

Asked if he accepted the Morgan affair had damaged the government, Peters said, "Isn't that rather obvious. If you have a campaign mounted about one member of the government saying that he is guilty of all sorts of heinous crimes, that would harm the government. Yes it has."
He said he saw the ATN saga and the fact Morgan sought money for an interview and misled Peters as one event.

"I see them all as one event. If the first event had not happened the second event would certainly not have happened. He would have had no occasion to (ask for the money for an interview) would he?" Peters said.
"If the SFO report is a complete vindication of him and the behaviour and allegations you made against him, you (the media) will be the ones with excuses," Peters said.
He said he would not discuss responses to hypotheticasl results of the SFO report.
Prime Minister Jim Bolger said he had accepted Morgan's apology.
"I have accepted his apology," Bolger told Reuters as he left the debating chamber.
Morgan refused to comment as he left the chamber.
